question: Who turned mono no aware, the pathos of passing things, into the key to Japanese literature?
answer: Motoori Norinaga, an 18th-century scholar who worked as a doctor. In his commentaries on The Tale of Genji, completed in the 1790s, he argued the novel meant not to teach morals but to make readers feel the sadness of transient things. A phrase from Heian poetry became a national aesthetic on one reader's desk.
move: A tradition's defining idea often turns out to have one later editor.
reference: Keene, World Within Walls: Japanese Literature of the Pre-Modern Era 1600-1867, Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1976
